deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous folio reduces meridian zenith distances of γ Ursae (from the declination ≈ 72°28', this is γ Ursae Minoris, Pherkad) observed at upper and lower culmination at Göttingen. There Gauss forms half the sum of the two readings, (20°56'48.826" + 55°59'29.060")/2 = 38°28'8.943", which gives the latitude φ = 90° − 38°28'8.943" = 51°31'51.057". He forms half the difference, giving the declination δ = 90° − (55°59'29.060" − 20°56'48.826")/2 = 72°28'39.883". He then compares with catalogue values ('Br', 'Pi', 'Be', probably Bradley, Piazzi, Bessel).

This page, headed 'γ Ursae an Reichenbachs Kreise' (γ Ursae at Reichenbach's circle), begins the same exercise with a different instrument.

- Nov 27: one circle reading, 20°24'46.05". No reduction is attached.
- Dec 7, lower culmination: reading 56°29'42.25". Gauss adds a correction of +91.90" and gets 56°31'14.15".
- Dec 7, upper culmination: reading 21°27'20.20". Gauss adds +24.15" and gets 21°27'44.35".

The corrections behave like astronomical refraction r ≈ k·tan z with k ≈ 60.8". The mean-refraction constant is about 57–58"; a larger value is plausible on a cold December night. Checks: 60.8·tan(56.52°) ≈ 92.0" and 60.8·tan(21.46°) ≈ 23.9". So the two corrected numbers are refraction-corrected zenith distances (circle readings) of the two culminations.

The page stops here. The next step, which I am supplying, would repeat the previous folio's reduction:
- Half-difference: (56°31'14.15" − 21°27'44.35")/2 = 17°31'44.90", so δ ≈ 72°28'15.10".
- Half-sum: 38°59'29.25". This exceeds the previous page's 38°28'8.94" by about 31'20". That offset is consistent with a different index/zero point on this circle, so the latitude cannot be obtained without the index correction.

The Nov 27 reading (20°24'46") does not pair with the Dec 7 readings on the same zero. It was probably taken with another circle setting or is unreduced.
errors: The page is an unfinished reduction. The half-difference implied by the Dec 7 numbers (δ ≈ 72°28'15") differs by about 25" from the 72°28'39.9" of the previous folio. This cannot be resolved from the page; possible causes are a different instrument, uncorrected flexure or division errors, or the corrections not being purely refraction.

results.what: Refraction correction of meridian zenith distances of a circumpolar star at upper and lower culmination (Reichenbach circle)
results.modern_name: Astronomical refraction reduction; determination of latitude and declination from upper/lower culminations of a circumpolar star
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice of 18th–19th c. positional astronomy (Bradley, Bessel and others)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine observational bookkeeping: two circle readings with refraction added, part of Gauss's well-documented Göttingen latitude and declination work with Reichenbach instruments.

checkable.asserts: Both corrections are consistent with refraction proportional to tan z with a common constant ≈ 61" (within ~1")
Previous folio's declination 72°28'39.883" follows from its upper and lower culmination readings

transcription_corrections: Heading reads 'γ Ursae an Reichenbachs Kreise'; this is consistent with γ Ursae Minoris (δ ≈ 72°28') rather than γ UMa.
In '21.27.20.20' the final digits are overwritten in the manuscript; 20.20 is confirmed by the sum 20.20 + 24.15 = 44.35.
